title: K-injective resolutions determine a natural Roos comparison
statement: Let A be an abelian category with countable products and inverse limits, with a derived category for A and its natural-number inverse towers. Suppose the tower category is Grothendieck abelian and inverse limit is additive. Two families of isomorphisms from the localization of the strict positive-difference Roos complex [def-weil-strict-roos-model] to derived inverse limit [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison] are equal if both are natural in the tower complex and they agree on every K-injective tower complex. The module also transports the existing exact-products comparison to the strict positive-difference convention and proves its normalized uniqueness as private helpers.

source.place: Localization returned Step 6: strict Roos comparison, uniqueness by K-injective resolutions.

proof.text: Given a tower complex M, take the functorial K-injective resolution q : M → I. The localized q and hence its image under derived inverse limit are isomorphisms. Naturality identifies each comparison postcomposed with this image with the Roos image of q followed by its comparison on I. Equality on I and cancellation prove equality on M. No boundedness or nonzero hypothesis is used.

The retained proved private normalization first applies ExactProductsRoos.comparisonIso to rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ. Transport along the existing signIso and ordinaryIso identifies the normalized positive-difference inclusion. On K-injectives this inclusion is invertible by its unit equation; cancel it to identify any other normalized comparison. Apply the proved public resolution uniqueness lemma to extend to all complexes.

For checking time, retain the already-proved coordinate product comparison and its uniqueness, uniqueness of the universal exact left-derived comparison, and its exact counit normalization as private helpers. These are the parent's original categorical calculations, with unchanged statements and complete proofs.

proof_origin.place: Strict Roos normalization and uniqueness; extraction of the already-proved generic argument to keep the parent below its compile-time limit.

theorem sfRoosComparison_ext
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [HasCountableProducts A]
    [HasLimitsOfShape ℕᵒᵖ A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A)]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A)]
    [(lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A).Additive]
    (e e' : ∀ M : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ,
      DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (strictRoosComplex M) ≅
        (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A).rightDerivedFunctor.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj M))
    (he : ∀ (M N : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ) (a : M ⟶ N),
      DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map (roosF.map a) ≫ (e N).hom =
        (e M).hom ≫ (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A).rightDerivedFunctor.map
          (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map a))
    (he' : ∀ (M N : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ) (a : M ⟶ N),
      DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map (roosF.map a) ≫ (e' N).hom =
        (e' M).hom ≫ (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A).rightDerivedFunctor.map
          (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map a))
    (hI : ∀ (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective], e I = e' I) :
    e = e'
